title: loading navigation properties eager explicit lazy and N+1
concepts: Related data can be projected, eagerly included, explicitly loaded, or lazily loaded. The right strategy depends on which data is needed, the number of database round trips, result duplication, and context lifetime.

Include and ThenInclude request related entity graphs. Projection often transfers fewer columns and expresses a read model directly; filtered include and tracking fix-up can produce surprising navigation contents.

Lazy loading can silently issue queries during property access and create N+1 behavior. Explicit loading makes round trips visible; eager loading can still cause cartesian explosion when several collections are joined.
Split queries avoid some row duplication by issuing multiple SQL queries, but add round trips and can observe concurrent changes between queries unless transaction isolation provides a stable view.
Query shape and behavior vary by provider. Measure SQL, returned rows, transferred bytes, and database round trips rather than judging by the LINQ expression alone.

versionNotes.edition: EF Core 11.0.0 released 2026-11-10; related-data behavior checked 2026-11-16
items: EF Core 11 improves SQL for reference-navigation includes: it prunes redundant to-one joins in split collection queries and removes redundant reference keys from ORDER BY clauses. This does not remove split-query round trips, consistency, or buffering tradeoffs. EF Core 11 What's New currently carries a stale development banner; use final release notes for release status.
